item.title: Reliance rebuts Musk's allegations, says rules apply equally to all
item.description: Reliance said it welcomes domestic and foreign competition, stressing that all satellite service providers, including Jio, must follow the same regulatory approval process ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Companies / News / Reliance rebuts Musk's allegations, says rules apply equally to all

Reliance rebuts Musk's allegations, says rules apply equally to all Reliance said it welcomes domestic and foreign competition, stressing that all satellite service providers, including Jio, must follow the same regulatory approval process

Rejecting suggestions that it was opposed to competition, the company cited the growth of its telecom business since its launch in 2016 | Photo: Bloomberg

Our Bureau New Delhi 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 16 2026 | 8:47 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Reliance Industries on Friday said it has never feared competition and that India's regulatory framework treats domestic and foreign companies equally, responding to recent criticism by billionaire Elon Musk over delays in the launch of his satellite internet service, Starlink, in the country.   "In light of recent remarks about Reliance and the Indian market, we wish to place the facts on record," the company said in a statement.   "Like every Indian enterprise, Reliance has grown in an India that welcomes investment and innovation, homegrown or international, that improve the lives of the people," it said.   The company maintained that India's openness to investment was underpinned by the rule of law, pointing out that its own satellite services were also awaiting regulatory approvals.

"That openness rests on the rule of law. As the Government of India has stated, it applies the same process to every applicant, Indian or foreign. Jio's own satellite services await clearances," Reliance said. Also Read

Jio Platforms set to bring India's biggest IPO on Oct 21, seeks ₹30,213 cr

Ahead of Starlink in queue for satcom nod, says Sunil Bharti Mittal

Rejecting suggestions that it was opposed to competition, the company cited the growth of its telecom business since its launch in 2016.   "At Reliance, we have never feared competition. We see it as the truest test of who serves the customer best," it said.   The company pointed out that Jio had entered India's crowded telecom market in 2016 without a single customer and had since expanded its subscriber base to over 530 million.

"In just ten years, Jio has earned the trust of over 530 million customers and given Indians some of the best digital infrastructure and most affordable data in the world," the statement said. What Elon Musk said about Reliance The response comes after Musk repeatedly targeted Reliance Industries Chairman Mukesh Ambani over delays in Starlink's commercial launch in India, accusing him of seeking to protect his position in the country's telecom market.   On October 11, Musk renewed his attack, accusing Ambani's online supporters of "absurd hypocrisy and hyperbole" for making contradictory arguments about Starlink's competitiveness.   In a post on X, Musk questioned how Starlink could simultaneously be considered too expensive to compete with Jio's low-cost services and a serious competitive threat to the company.

He argued that allowing Starlink to operate would increase consumer choice and benefit Indian customers. Musk also said that even if additional competition reduced Ambani's profits, it would not drive him out of business.   Earlier, Musk had sarcastically addressed the Reliance chairman as "Prime Minister Ambani", alleging that he wielded influence over Starlink's entry into India.   "Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realising that you are the real boss of India," Musk wrote on X, accusing Ambani of seeking to preserve a monopoly and questioning whether Starlink would be allowed to compete.   Musk has argued that Starlink could improve internet connectivity in remote and underserved areas, expand access to education and digital markets, and provide essential communications during natural disasters.

The controversy has also drawn a response from the government, which has rejected suggestions that the regulatory approval process favours any particular company.   Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said on October 9 that India does not allow monopolies in any sector and that the Department of Telecommunications follows a technology-agnostic approach.   He said three companies — Starlink, Reliance Jio's satellite venture Jio Satcom, and Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb — had secured satellite communication licences but would be permitted to begin operations only after fulfilling the prescribed security requirements and regulatory milestones.   The government has maintained that its authorisation framework for telecom and satellite services is fair and non-discriminatory, dismissing allegations of selective treatment as baseless.

The dispute comes as satellite broadband providers seek to enter India's internet services market, where Starlink and domestic telecom operators are preparing to compete for customers, particularly in areas underserved by conventional networks.   More From This Section

item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Trump says he is talking to Russia and China about denuclearisation

Trump says he is talking to Russia and China about denuclearisation Russia has the most stored nuclear warheads followed by the United States and China, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute

US President Donald Trump (Photo:PTI)

Reuters 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 16 2026 | 8:36 AM IST

US President ??Donald Trump said on Thursday Washington is holding talks with Moscow and Beijing aimed ??at denuclearising the countries with the biggest stockpiles of nuclear weapons.   Russia has the most stored nuclear warheads followed by the United States and China, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. The US outpaces Russia on its number of deployed warheads.   During an interview with Newsmax, Trump said he expects China to "catch up" with the US within the next five years. "The whole thing is a shame, because I'd love to denuclearise if possible, but we're actually talking to Russia about that, and we're talking to China about that denuclearization," Trump told the outlet.

Newsmax reported that Trump had spoken with Chinese President Xi ??Jinping about denuclearisation.   Also Read

India gains ground in cleantech manufacturing as supply chains diversify premium

Trump's comments come months after the Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty expired earlier this year.   The New START treaty signed in 2010 allowed one single extension, which was agreed by former President Joe Biden and Russian President Vladimir Putin for five years. Any new extension would require an executive decision to voluntarily extend the limits of the treaty.   (Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)     More From This Section

item.title: CAS review: Sebi announces last 30-minute VWAP method for settlement
item.description: Sebi has revised the closing auction session framework, adopting the last 30-minute VWAP for derivatives settlement and changing trading hours from December 7, 2026.
item.dc:creator: Khushboo Tiwari
item.content:encoded: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) on Thursday announced the much-awaited revisions to the closing auction session (CAS) framework, introducing changes to the settlement methodology, trading timings, and the transition of unexecuted iceberg orders. An iceberg order is a large order split into smaller orders where only a fraction of the total quantity is visible in the order book displayed to the public. The revised framework will take effect from December 7, 2026, except for changes relating to the transition of unexecuted limit and iceberg orders from the continuous trading session (CTS) to CAS, which will come into force from February 8, 2027. Retaining the earlier method, the settlement price of index derivatives will be based on the volume-weighted average prices (VWAP) of constituent securities during the last 30 minutes of the CTS (3.00 pm to 3.30 pm) in the equity cash segment.For expiring stock derivatives, clearing corporations will determine settlement prices using the VWAP of the underlying stock during the last 30 minutes of the CTS across all stock exchanges. Exchanges will provide the VWAP and quantity traded to clearing corporations and continuously disseminate indicative values to market participants in real time during this period. Under the revised timings, CAS will operate as a separate 10-minute session from 3:30 pm to 3:40 pm on all trading days. The order-entry period will close randomly between 3:38 pm and 3:40 pm. Trading in index derivatives will continue until 3:45 pm on regular trading days, but contracts expiring that day will stop trading at 3:30 pm. Trading in stock derivatives will continue until 3:45 pm, including on expiry days. The post-close session in the cash segment will run from 3:50 pm to 4 pm, with trades executed at the closing prices of securities. CAS became effective on August 3 and saw an uproar from the trading community over the settlement price, sharp spikes, and low liquidity. The latest changes were announced following a consultation paper that received over 20,000 suggestions, which was followed by deliberations of the market regulator’s Secondary Market Advisory Committee on Thursday. The regulator had also proposed a blended mechanism, on which several market participants had raised concerns, given the low liquidity in the window.  Traders and brokers had favoured the 30-minute VWAP method stating that participants were more familiar with this mechanism and that it was more transparent and operationally well understood. On Thursday, Sebi also specified how unexecuted orders will move from the CTS to CAS. Pending limit orders will generally be carried forward, except stop-loss orders and orders priced beyond the applicable CAS price bands. Unexecuted iceberg orders within the applicable price bands will be converted into fully disclosed limit orders (at fixed/pre-determined price), unless market participants opt out when placing the original orders. These converted orders will have lower time priority than other limit orders carried forward from the continuous session, but higher priority than limit orders placed during CAS. At present, CAS is a 20 minute window from 3:15 pm to 3:35 pm where the reference price calculation and transition from CTS to CAS happens from 3:15 pm to 3:20 pm. In this period, no order entry is allowed. The next five minutes order entry period remains. From 3.25 pm to 3.30 pm, the order entry period is restricted to limit orders only, and no modifications or cancellations of market orders are allowed. In this period, trading closes randomly in the last two minutes. In its consultation paper, Sebi had also proposed prohibiting cancellation of limit orders placed beyond 1 per cent range of the reference price during CAS. However, the regulator skipped this change in the final circular. What’s new Stock derivatives’ settlement prices will use underlying stocks’ volume-weighted average prices across exchangesCAS will run from 3:30 pm to 3:40 pm, with random closureExpiring index derivatives will stop trading at 3:30 pm; stock derivatives at 3:45 pmIceberg orders will become fully disclosed limit orders unless participants opt out

item.title: Google DeepMind ties up with ICRISAT to develop plant genome atlas
item.description: The open-access catalogue will use AI to help breeders identify promising plant combinations faster, while the partnership will also support genome mapping for other crops ...
item.dc:creator: Aashish Aryan
item.content:encoded: Google DeepMind and Google.org have partnered with Hyderabad-headquartered International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT) to launch an open-access global public genetic atlas aimed at identifying the most promising plant combinations, particularly in sorghum, Google India said. “The resulting AI-supported genetic catalogue is aimed at helping breeders and researchers across the world to develop more resilient and productive sorghum varieties faster than traditional methods, which can involve decade-long trial-and-error processes,” the company said in a blog post. Google DeepMind will also support a three-year postdoctoral fellowship at ICRISAT to help develop tools that can map and characterise genomes for other crops and pulses such as chickpea, groundnut and pigeon pea, the company said. “We aim for this collaboration to unlock the global potential of indigenous climate-resilient crops like sorghum, and to empower the agri ecosystem with cutting-edge tools that strengthen global food security and safeguard present and future generations,” Stanford Blade, deputy director general of research and innovation at ICRISAT, said. Separately, Google is expanding access to its Agricultural Understanding Models to enable developers, startups and researchers to build customised solutions for hyperlocal farming challenges and strengthen agricultural resilience, the company said. The move is aimed at widening access to AI tools that can be used to address local agricultural conditions and improve decision-making across the farm ecosystem. Google’s AI Educator Series, first launched in May this year in partnership with five states, is now being expanded to Bihar and Madhya Pradesh. The series will also be made available as a free online resource accessible to users across the country, Google India said. Google.org, Google’s philanthropic arm, will also provide $15 million to The/Nudge to support the growth of micro, small and medium enterprises in India. “This initiative will fund the development of scalable AI tools to expand small enterprises' access to formal credit, market discovery, and compliance,” the company said.
